topic.title: Neural Expressivity, Learnability, and Compute Bounds
topic.overview: Neural-network theory distinguishes which functions an architecture can represent, which can be learned efficiently, and which generalize from finite examples. Width, depth, weight magnitude, connectivity, and precision all enter these questions. The represented work also studies what approximation is lost when computation is pruned or stopped early.
topic.whyItMatters: A representation theorem alone does not explain successful training. Likewise, a smaller network may retain accuracy only for particular data geometry or parameter configurations. Sharp bounds help identify where architectural intuition is justified and where proof barriers remain.
topic.evolution: The collection reaches back to 1987 connections between connectivity and problem complexity. Later results examine width, learning hardness, and depth separation. Recent analyses connect partial computation with accuracy and expose barriers inherited from circuit complexity. These results offer complementary limits rather than one scalar measure of neural capability.
openQuestions: Which expressivity advantages are reachable by practical optimization?
Can compute–accuracy guarantees remain informative for trained networks outside idealized asymptotic models?

papers.tldr: New NTK spectral bounds support memorization and optimization guarantees for deep networks with sublinear widths and near-linear parameter counts.

papers.title: Most Activation Functions Can Win the Lottery Without Excessive Depth
papers.tldr: A new construction shows that depth L+1 can suffice to contain lottery-ticket approximations of depth-L networks, with logarithmic overparameterization and broad activation support.

papers.title: Neural Network Architecture Beyond Width and Depth
papers.tldr: NestNets introduce recursively nested activations, yielding stronger approximation rates than standard ReLU networks at comparable parameter counts.

papers.title: Non-Gaussian Tensor Programs
papers.tldr: Non-Gaussian Tensor Programs characterize when wide-network limits depend on the distributions used to initialize parameters.

papers.title: On Measuring Excess Capacity in Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Complexity bounds and experiments suggest networks can retain comparable training error under substantial constraints on weight-based capacity.

papers.title: On the Generalization Power of the Overfitted Three-Layer Neural Tangent Kernel Model
papers.tldr: For a specified learnable function set, three-layer NTK test-error bounds improve with width and favor expansion of the hidden layer nearer the output.

papers.title: Real-Valued Backpropagation is Unsuitable for Complex-Valued Neural Networks
papers.tldr: For most complex activations, real-valued backpropagation makes infinite-width complex networks train like ordinary real networks.

papers.title: Size and depth of monotone neural networks: interpolation and approximation
papers.tldr: Depth-four monotone networks can fit any finite monotone dataset, but positive-parameter constraints can impose substantial neuron-count costs.

papers.title: Statistically Meaningful Approximation: a Case Study on Approximating Turing Machines with Transformers
papers.tldr: The paper strengthens neural approximation theory with learnability requirements and derives sample-complexity guarantees for circuits and time-bounded Turing machines.

papers.title: The Sample Complexity of One-Hidden-Layer Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Spectral norm control alone generally fails to give width-independent uniform convergence, but suffices under particular smoothness or convolutional-architecture conditions.

papers.title: Transition to Linearity of General Neural Networks with Directed Acyclic Graph Architecture
papers.tldr: Feedforward networks on arbitrary directed acyclic graphs exhibit transition to linearity as a connectivity-based measure of width tends to infinity.

papers.title: A Fast, Well-Founded Approximation to the Empirical Neural Tangent Kernel
papers.tldr: The paper gives theoretical support and empirical evidence for a much smaller approximation to the empirical neural tangent kernel.

papers.title: Efficient Parametric Approximations of Neural Network Function Space Distance
papers.tldr: LAFTR compactly approximates differences between ReLU networks’ outputs, supporting continual learning and data analysis without repeated full-dataset processing.

papers.title: Hidden Symmetries of ReLU Networks
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes hidden parameter redundancies in ReLU networks and studies how their occurrence varies with architecture.

papers.title: How Powerful are Shallow Neural Networks with Bandlimited Random Weights?
papers.tldr: Bounded random hidden weights can impose irreducible approximation error, so shallow random networks need suitable feature distributions.

papers.title: Minimum Width of Leaky-ReLU Neural Networks for Uniform Universal Approximation
papers.tldr: The paper establishes the exact minimum width for uniform universal approximation by arbitrarily deep leaky-ReLU networks on compact domains.

papers.title: Multi-Layer Neural Networks as Trainable Ladders of Hilbert Spaces
papers.tldr: Neural Hilbert Ladders describe multilayer networks through adaptive function spaces, linking representation, generalization, and infinite-width training dynamics.

papers.title: Nearly-tight Bounds for Deep Kernel Learning
papers.tldr: The paper derives nearly tight generalization bounds for deep kernel models with mild dependence on network depth.

papers.title: On Enhancing Expressive Power via Compositions of Single Fixed-Size ReLU Network
papers.tldr: Repeatedly composing a single fixed-size ReLU network yields provable approximation power that increases with the number of repetitions.

papers.title: Provable Data Subset Selection For Efficient Neural Networks Training
papers.tldr: The paper constructs weighted coresets for radial basis function networks and uses them to derive provable subset selection for neural-network training.

papers.title: Quantitative Universal Approximation Bounds for Deep Belief Networks
papers.tldr: Deep belief networks with binary hidden units have conditional universal density-approximation guarantees and sharp error bounds tied to hidden-unit count.

papers.title: Complex-valued Neurons Can Learn More but Slower than Real-valued Neurons via Gradient Descent
papers.tldr: Complex-valued neurons can learn a broader class of single-neuron targets, but learning real-valued targets can be much slower.

papers.title: Computational Complexity of Learning Neural Networks: Smoothness and Degeneracy
papers.tldr: Conditional hardness results show that smoothing and non-degeneracy do not suffice for efficient learning in the studied neural-network settings.

papers.title: Globally injective and bijective neural operators
papers.tldr: The paper establishes conditions for injective and surjective neural operators, including preservation of injectivity in finite-rank network implementations.

papers.title: Most Neural Networks Are Almost Learnable
papers.tldr: Random constant-depth Xavier networks admit polynomial-time approximate learning for fixed error tolerance on the stated spherical input domain.

papers.title: Neural Injective Functions for Multisets, Measures and Graphs via a Finite Witness Theorem
papers.tldr: Neural moments can distinguish multisets injectively with analytic non-polynomial activations, but piecewise-linear moments cannot, and distance preservation has fundamental limits.

papers.title: New Complexity-Theoretic Frontiers of Tractability for Neural Network Training
papers.tldr: New algorithmic upper bounds expand the known cases where linear and ReLU neural networks can be trained optimally and efficiently.

papers.title: On the Role of Noise in the Sample Complexity of Learning Recurrent Neural Networks: Exponential Gaps for Long Sequences
papers.tldr: Even tiny independent Gaussian neuron noise produces a logarithmic-versus-linear separation in sequence-length dependence for the studied RNN sample-complexity bounds.

papers.title: Optimal approximation using complex-valued neural networks
papers.tldr: The paper establishes approximation rates for a broad class of complex-valued networks and proves conditional optimality and dimensionality barriers.

papers.title: Polynomially Over-Parameterized Convolutional Neural Networks Contain Structured Strong Winning Lottery Tickets
papers.tldr: The paper proves that a broad class of over-parameterized random convolutional networks contains structured subnetworks approximating sufficiently smaller networks.

papers.title: Should Under-parameterized Student Networks Copy or Average Teacher Weights?
papers.tldr: Under specific shallow-network assumptions, the best copy-average configuration copies individual teacher neurons and averages the remainder in one neuron.

papers.title: Structure of universal formulas
papers.tldr: A hierarchy of expressiveness reveals structural limits and separates arbitrary finite-set approximation from universal approximation across a domain.

papers.title: Training Fully Connected Neural Networks is $\exists\mathbb{R}$-Complete
papers.tldr: Exactly optimizing even small fully connected ReLU networks is ∃R-complete, and some rational datasets require algebraic optimal weights.

papers.title: Training Neural Networks is NP-Hard in Fixed Dimension
papers.tldr: Training two-layer networks remains NP-hard in two dimensions, while convex ReLU maps admit a combined-parameter tractability result.

papers.title: Characterizing ResNet’s Universal Approximation Capability
papers.tldr: The paper derives order-optimal approximation rates for constant-width ResNets across several important function classes.

papers.title: Defining Neural Network Architecture through Polytope Structures of Datasets
papers.tldr: The paper connects neural network width bounds to dataset geometry and infers compact polytope descriptions from trained networks.

papers.title: Efficient PAC Learnability of Dynamical Systems Over Multilayer Networks
papers.tldr: The paper establishes efficient PAC learning for multilayer network dynamics and tightly characterizes model complexity for almost all multilayer graphs.

papers.title: Exploring the Complexity of Deep Neural Networks through Functional Equivalence
papers.tldr: Accounting for parameterizations that represent the same function yields tighter network complexity analysis and insight into why wider networks can train more easily.

papers.title: Neural Networks Learn Statistics of Increasing Complexity
papers.tldr: Statistical matching and targeted data edits support the view that networks learn simpler distributional features before higher-order correlations.

papers.title: On dimensionality of feature vectors in MPNNs
papers.tldr: With any non-polynomial analytic activation, one-dimensional MPNN features suffice to match the Weisfeiler–Leman test’s distinguishing power.

papers.title: On the Feasibility of Single-Pass Full-Capacity Learning in Linear Threshold Neurons with Binary Input Vectors
papers.tldr: Span rules cannot combine single-pass learning with full theoretical capacity for the studied binary-input threshold neuron.

papers.title: ReLU Network with Width $d+\mathcalO(1)$ Can Achieve Optimal Approximation Rate
papers.tldr: Narrow ReLU networks achieve optimal approximation rates at width d+1 for finite Lp norms, while width d+11 suffices for the uniform norm.

papers.title: The Effect of Weight Precision on the Neuron Count in Deep ReLU Networks
papers.tldr: Higher weight precision can reduce ReLU neuron counts through expensive preprocessing, but the savings change when precision and construction time are counted.

papers.title: Vocabulary for Universal Approximation: A Linguistic Perspective of Mapping Compositions
papers.tldr: A finite vocabulary of O(d²) mappings can approximate any continuous d-dimensional mapping on a compact domain through suitable compositions.

papers.title: A two-scale Complexity Measure for Deep Learning Models
papers.tldr: 2sED is a model-capacity measure with a conditional generalization bound and a scalable lower approximation for Markovian models.

papers.title: Matching the Statistical Query Lower Bound for $k$-Sparse Parity Problems with Sign Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.tldr: The paper proves that sign-based stochastic gradient training can solve sparse parity with complexity characterized as matching statistical-query lower bounds.

papers.title: On the Sparsity of the Strong Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
papers.tldr: A fixed-size random subset sum bound yields strong lottery ticket results that also guarantee subnetwork sparsity.

papers.title: Provable Tempered Overfitting of Minimal Nets and Typical Nets
papers.tldr: The paper proves tempered overfitting for minimal and randomly selected binary-weight deep networks that perfectly fit noisy training data.

papers.title: Separation and Bias of Deep Equilibrium Models on Expressivity and Learning Dynamics
papers.tldr: The paper establishes conditional expressivity advantages and learning biases of deep equilibrium models, suggesting possible benefits for certain high-frequency functions.

papers.title: Approximation to Smooth Functions by Low-Rank Swish Networks
papers.tldr: Fixed-depth, low-rank Swish networks can approximate a specified class of smooth functions arbitrarily well while reducing computational cost.

papers.title: Exact Upper and Lower Bounds for the Output Distribution of Neural Networks with Random Inputs
papers.tldr: ReLU-based network bounds yield guaranteed bounds on output distributions under random inputs, converging to the true distribution as resolution increases.

papers.title: Floating-Point Neural Networks Can Represent Almost All Floating-Point Functions
papers.tldr: Floating-point networks can represent every floating-point function on broad domains when their first layer distinguishes inputs and their activations satisfy mild conditions.

papers.title: Minimum Width for Universal Approximation using Squashable Activation Functions
papers.tldr: The paper establishes exact universal-approximation width bounds for broad classes of squashable activations, with a qualified scalar-case exception.

papers.title: The Power of Random Features and the Limits of Distribution-Free Gradient Descent
papers.tldr: Anything learnable distribution-free by the analyzed mini-batch gradient method can also be approximated with polynomially many random features, with high probability.

papers.title: Approximation and Generalization Abilities of Score-based Neural Network Generative Models for Sub-Gaussian Distributions
papers.tldr: The paper establishes score-model approximation and learning guarantees under weaker distributional assumptions, with near-optimal rates under additional smoothness.

papers.title: Bounds on the computational complexity of neurons due to dendritic morphology
papers.tldr: Experiments link dendritic size and structure to a single neuron's learnable functions, reliability, and ability to adapt.

papers.title: Depth-Bounds for Neural Networks via the Braid Arrangement
papers.tldr: For braid-fan-compatible ReLU networks, the paper proves growing depth requirements for exact maximum computation and sharpens related maxout constructions.

papers.title: Effective Neural Approximations for Geometric Optimization Problems
papers.tldr: Geometry-aligned neural networks approximate point-set extent measures with guarantees and parameter counts independent of input size.

papers.title: Generalization Bounds for Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) and Enhanced KANs with Lower Lipschitz Complexity
papers.tldr: The paper derives complexity-based generalization bounds for KANs and uses them to design LipKANs with tighter bounds and improved empirical generalization.

papers.title: Identifiability of Deep Polynomial Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper establishes conditional identifiability results for deep polynomial networks by linking architecture and activation degree to tensor-decomposition uniqueness.

papers.title: Infinite-Width Limit of a Single Attention Layer: Analysis via Tensor Programs
papers.tldr: A single attention layer has a non-Gaussian infinite-width limit under standard scaling, although it is Gaussian conditional on random similarity scores.

papers.title: Minimum Width for Deep, Narrow MLP: A Diffeomorphism Approach
papers.tldr: A geometric framework yields new upper bounds and exact minimum widths for universal approximation by deep, narrow neural networks.

papers.title: Online Learning of Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes margin-based online learnability for sign-activation networks and identifies restrictions that avoid dimension-dependent mistake bounds.

papers.title: Optimal Minimum Width for the Universal Approximation of Continuously Differentiable Functions by Deep Narrow MLPs
papers.tldr: The paper establishes optimal widths in certain cases for deep networks approximating both continuously differentiable functions and their first derivatives.

papers.title: Quantitative convergence of trained neural networks to Gaussian processes
papers.tldr: Explicit bounds quantify how trained shallow networks approach Gaussian processes as width increases, including the effects of architecture and training dynamics.

papers.title: Reproducing Kernel Banach Space Models for Neural Networks with Application to Rademacher Complexity Analysis
papers.tldr: An exact Banach-space model yields a width-independent neural-network complexity bound and, under parameter constraints, a bound independent of both width and depth.

papers.title: The Computational Complexity of Counting Linear Regions in ReLU Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Counting ReLU linear regions is generally computationally hard, even in shallow networks, although some definitions permit polynomial-space algorithms.

papers.title: The Cost of Robustness: Tighter Bounds on Parameter Complexity for Robust Memorization in ReLU Nets
papers.tldr: Tighter bounds characterize how ReLU-network parameter requirements grow as robust memorization demands larger neighborhoods relative to label separation.

papers.title: Any-dimensional invariant universality
papers.tldr: A limit-space framework defines universality across input sizes and exposes architectural gaps that simple modifications can repair.

papers.title: Floating-Point Networks with Automatic Differentiation Can Represent Almost All Floating-Point Functions and Their Gradients
papers.tldr: The paper establishes broad representability results for floating-point network values and automatically computed gradients, including simultaneous gradients under mild conditions.

papers.title: Generalization and Scaling Laws for Mixture-of-ExpertsTransformers
papers.tldr: The paper derives MoE generalization and scaling results by separating active parameter capacity from the additional complexity of routing.

papers.title: Learning High-Dimensional Parity Functions with Product Networks using Gradient Descent
papers.tldr: Compact product networks can learn high-dimensional parity efficiently under sparse Bernoulli inputs and suitable hyperparameter choices.

papers.title: $\mathcalO(\log N)$ Latent Dimension Suffices for Universal Approximation of Permutation-invariant Function
papers.tldr: For Wasserstein-stable set functions, a constructive approximation bound needs only logarithmic growth in latent dimension with set size.

papers.title: On Minimum Depth and Width of Floating-Point Neural Networks for Representing Floating-Point Functions
papers.tldr: Floating-point ReLU networks require depth three for full-domain universal representation, with minimum width tightly bounded by input dimension.

papers.title: Rational Neural Networks have Expressivity Advantages
papers.tldr: Trainable rational activations offer provable approximation-efficiency advantages and match or outperform fixed activations in the reported practical comparisons.

papers.title: Theoretical Guarantees for One-Shot Magnitude Pruning and Compute-Adaptive Early Exit
papers.tldr: A unified theory relates pruning and early-exit accuracy to how closely partial computations match full computations.

papers.title: Verified SHAP: Provable Bounds for Exact Shapley Values of Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Verified SHAP uses neural network verification to tighten provable attribution bounds and recover exact values on substantially larger search spaces.

papers.title: Why ReLU? A Bit-Model Dichotomy for Deep Network Training
papers.tldr: A finite-bit analysis shows that ReLU permits polynomial-time backpropagation while polynomial activations can make even gradient computation hard.
